# The dungeons' art: prompts for ChatGPT (v2.3.3561)

<!-- GENERATED by tools/world/dungeon-art-prompts.mjs: edit the script, then run it. -->

The owner, on the dungeons' bare arenas: "instead of code drawn walls give prompt for me to give chatGPT to draw dungeon walls and any other assets you think would be good".

Each dungeon gets three pictures: its **entrance** (today a dark oval drawn in code), its **walls** (today one flat colour), and a sheet of **things to stand inside** its arena (today a bare floor). One more, the **boss's treasure chest**, is shared by all four.

- **One chat each.** Attach what each item lists, and never the bro (docs/WORLD-BIBLE.md §6): he is simpler pixel art than the world, and ChatGPT copies what it sees.
- **Send each result in chat**, and a session fits it in: the "In the game" line says where it goes.
- **Your style key** is the one you attach to every Object Studio chat. `docs/art/dungeon-floors-key.png` is in the repo; it shows the four arenas' floors, so the walls belong on them.
- Every prompt is the Object Studio's own words (`public/tools/style/bible.js`, `public/tools/objects/prompts.js`), so the pictures come back in the size and style its cutters expect.

## Make these first: the Goo Grotto and the chest (4 chats)

The Goo Grotto is the one dungeon a reviewer can reach in their first half hour: levels 1–5, about 30 seconds' walk from BroTown, in the middle of the slimes the Mayor's first quest sends you to. The other three are for levels 26–45.

### The Goo Grotto: dungeon entrance

- **In the game:** where the Verdant Wilds' dungeon starts (levels 1–5, on the way to the Mayor's first slimes). Today it is a dark oval drawn in code.
- **Attach:** your style key.
- **How:** ask for a wide 3:2 picture, as the Object Studio does. Send it in chat: a session cuts it out and draws it at the dungeon's mouth.

```text
A wide picture (3:2, landscape) of ONE object for BroTown, a top-down 2D action RPG: the entrance to a dungeon: a low, wide cave mouth in a mound of mossy green-grey rock, thick tree roots and hanging moss draped over its top and ferns at its sides, with sticky blue slime oozing out of the dark opening and dripping off its lip, which is wide enough for three people to walk in side by side. It is drawn whole in the middle of the picture, with plenty of background all round and nothing cut off. It stands on nothing: no ground, grass, path or shadow under or around it, and the place where it meets the ground is plain to see.

No text, letters or numbers anywhere. The background is ONE flat magenta colour (#FF00FF) everywhere, with no shading, gradient, texture, shadow or glow, so it can be cut away cleanly. Nothing in the picture is magenta or bright pink. No border.

Style: BroTown HD pixel art: crisp, modern high-definition pixel art on one clean square pixel grid, like Eastward or Sea of Stars. Every pixel is a hard-edged square: no blur, no anti-aliasing, no soft brushes and no smooth gradients. Each colour is shaded with 3 to 5 flat tones, in clusters of pixels rather than single stray ones, with shadows shifted toward cool blue-purple and highlights toward warm yellow. Every material is drawn as itself, so it can be told apart at a glance by its own texture and the shape of its highlights: grass in soft clumps of blades, packed earth with a few small stones, stone with hard-edged facets, chips and cracks, wood with grain lines and knots, metal with small, sharp, bright highlights, snow and ice in cool blues with crisp edges, and sand in soft, fine drifts. Texture comes from a few clear shapes and soft shading, never from noise, speckle or grain. Highlights are small clusters of pixels, never single stray ones. Soft, even daylight from the upper left. No shadows cast on the ground, and no glow, fog or lighting effects: the game adds those. The ground has no outlines. Anything that stands up has a one-pixel outline in a darker shade of its own colour, never black, lighter on the sunlit side. Moderate saturation, with the ground calm and mid-toned so characters stand out. Seen from a steep three-quarter top-down angle, with no perspective.

Attached is the game's style key. Match its pixel size, colours, shading and the way it draws each material exactly, but do not copy its tiles. Scale: a person standing here would be about one fifth as tall as this picture. It is about four and a half times as wide as a person is tall, so it fills about three fifths of the picture's width.
```

### The Foundry Dome: inside the arena

- **In the game:** 14 things to stand round the Foundry Dome's arena, where its storm slimes fight you. Today the arena is a bare floor.
- **Attach:** your style key.
- **Background:** magenta, as the Object Studio's pictures.
- **How:** one wide sprite sheet. Send it in chat: a session cuts every object out by the count in its rows (the Object Studio's object finder) and stands them round the arena's edges, clear of the middle where you fight and of the way out. The torches or lamps go either side of the way out.

```text
A wide picture (3:2, landscape): a SPRITE SHEET of 14 objects for BroTown, a top-down 2D action RPG, laid out in two neat rows and read like a page: each row left to right, the rows top to bottom. Every object stands on its own with plain background all round it: none touches another, and each kind's ones stay together, in the order given.

Row 1, left to right: two tesla coil towers, copper coils wound round iron posts on riveted iron bases, switched off, with no sparks (a tall one, a short one), each about as tall as a person; then two electric lamp posts with big glass bulbs, switched off (a straight one, a bent one), each about as tall as a person; then a workbench of dark iron covered in dials, levers, wires and one big red switch, with no writing or numbers on its dials, about one and a half times as wide as a person is tall; then three big glass jars with copper lids, full of bright blue liquid (a tall one, a round one, a cracked one leaking a little blue puddle), each about waist-high on a person.
Row 2, left to right: three iron pipes coming up out of the floor (an elbow with a valve wheel, a T-joint with a round gauge with no numbers, a cracked one), each about chest-high on a person; then three heaps of scrap metal (broken cogwheels, bent plates, a pile of loose bolts and springs), each about knee-high on a person.

Every object is drawn whole, at its true size beside the others, and stands on nothing: no ground, grass, path or shadow under or around it, the place where it meets the ground plain to see. Everything is built and used by Bros: well made, a little battered, with a proud repair or a dent here and there.

No text, letters or numbers anywhere. The background is ONE flat magenta colour (#FF00FF) everywhere, with no shading, gradient, texture, shadow or glow, so it can be cut away cleanly. Nothing in the picture is magenta or bright pink. No border.

Style: BroTown HD pixel art: crisp, modern high-definition pixel art on one clean square pixel grid, like Eastward or Sea of Stars. Every pixel is a hard-edged square: no blur, no anti-aliasing, no soft brushes and no smooth gradients. Each colour is shaded with 3 to 5 flat tones, in clusters of pixels rather than single stray ones, with shadows shifted toward cool blue-purple and highlights toward warm yellow. Every material is drawn as itself, so it can be told apart at a glance by its own texture and the shape of its highlights: grass in soft clumps of blades, packed earth with a few small stones, stone with hard-edged facets, chips and cracks, wood with grain lines and knots, metal with small, sharp, bright highlights, snow and ice in cool blues with crisp edges, and sand in soft, fine drifts. Texture comes from a few clear shapes and soft shading, never from noise, speckle or grain. Highlights are small clusters of pixels, never single stray ones. Soft, even daylight from the upper left. No shadows cast on the ground, and no glow, fog or lighting effects: the game adds those. The ground has no outlines. Anything that stands up has a one-pixel outline in a darker shade of its own colour, never black, lighter on the sunlit side. Moderate saturation, with the ground calm and mid-toned so characters stand out. Seen from a steep three-quarter top-down angle, with no perspective.

Attached is the game's style key. Match its pixel size, colours, shading and the way it draws each material exactly, but do not copy its tiles. Scale: a person standing here would be about one fifth as tall as this picture; each object is the size given in its row.
```

## Not dungeons, but worth it before the review

- **The keepers, sheet 1 of 2** (docs/ART-WISHLIST.md, "The keepers"): Woodworker Bro and Farmer Bro are two of the six townsfolk a new player meets in the first half hour (the tour, docs/specs/demo-quest-line.md), and today both are stand-in pictures a script made. That one sheet draws them both, with four more keepers.
- **The Foundry Slime** (docs/ART-WISHLIST.md, "Monsters"): the Foundry Dome's storm slimes are the starter slime recoloured. Worth making with the Foundry Dome's other pictures, so its fight looks like its own.

## When the pictures come back (for the session that fits them in)

- **Entrances:** cut out like any Object Studio picture (`public/tools/style/process.js`), drawn at the mouth (`src/rendering/wheelDoors.js`) at 2 px a game px, its foot at the mouth; the code's oval, glow and name stay until each one's picture is in.
- **Walls:** each strip made seamless by the Ground Studio's cut (`seamless` in process.js); the front along the arena's top wall, the top all round (`src/data/wheelDungeons.js` WHEEL_DUNGEON_FLOOR's `wall` colour today). Loaded behind the dungeon's loading screen with its floor and freed when you leave (CLAUDE.md, the zone-asset exception).
- **Inside:** cut by count (`objectsIn` in process.js, the rows' order naming each); stood round the edges and either side of the way out, never in the middle third where the fight is; the big ones solid at their feet, the flat ones (puddles, scrap, coins) walked over; loaded and freed with the arena like the walls.
- **The chest:** both pictures held with the arena; the shut one where the boss falls, the open one once its reward is taken.
